title: Scope sessions API to current user and companion in chatbot/api/sessions.py
description:
Modify chatbot/api/sessions.py to scope all session operations to the authenticated user and optionally to a companion. Apply get_current_user dependency and enforce user_id filtering on all session CRUD endpoints.

Before editing, inspect:
- AGENTS.md
- docs/plans_tasks.md
- docs/operations.md
- docs/architecture.md
- docs/PLANS/ACTIVE/CHATBOT/README.md
- docs/PLANS/ACTIVE/CHATBOT/DISPATCH.md
- chatbot/api/sessions.py (existing sessions API — understand current endpoints, router name, data store mechanism, request/response models)
- chatbot/auth/dependencies.py (created by task c.5 — get_current_user, CurrentUser, get_current_user_id)
- chatbot/db/models.py (updated by task c.4 — Session model with user_id and companion_id columns)
- chatbot/companions/companion.py (created by task c.3 — CompanionManager, CompanionResponse)

Do not infer APIs, constructor signatures, function names, module locations, or service topology from the task description alone. Inspect the referenced documents and existing implementation files first, then implement against the actual repository.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY chatbot/api/sessions.py. Do NOT modify any other file under any circumstance. Do NOT update documentation, READMEs, operations guides, or any code outside the listed path. If you believe other files need updating, ignore that impulse and finish the task with only the listed file modified. Out-of-scope edits will cause the task to be rejected.

Implementation details:

1. Open chatbot/api/sessions.py and understand:
   - Current endpoints: POST /, GET /{session_id}, DELETE /{session_id}.
   - Current data store: in-memory dict, database-backed, or other.
   - Import paths for existing models and utilities.
   - Router variable name and prefix.

2. Add user_id scoping to all endpoints:
   - Import `get_current_user` from chatbot.auth.dependencies.
   - Add `current_user: CurrentUser = Depends(get_current_user)` to every endpoint.
   - Modify all database queries to filter by user_id from current_user.
   - On GET /{session_id}: if the session is not found OR belongs to a different user, return 404 (not 403 — do not leak that the session exists for another user).
   - On DELETE /{session_id}: if the session is not found OR belongs to a different user, return 404.
   - On POST /: store user_id from current_user on the new session record.

3. Add companion_id support:
   - POST / accepts optional companion_id in the request body.
   - If companion_id is provided, validate it exists and is owned by the current user (use CompanionManager). If not, return 404.
   - Store companion_id on the session record.
   - GET / (list) accepts optional companion_id query parameter to filter sessions by companion.

4. Do NOT rename the router, change endpoint URL paths, or change HTTP methods.
acceptance_criteria: chatbot/api/sessions.py imports and uses get_current_user dependency on all endpoints
POST /sessions stores user_id from current_user in the session record
GET /sessions/{session_id} returns 404 when session belongs to a different user
GET /sessions (list) filters to only the current user's sessions
DELETE /sessions/{session_id} enforces user ownership before deletion
POST /sessions accepts optional companion_id and stores it
Existing endpoint paths, router name, and prefix are preserved
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: rename the router or change existing endpoint URL paths
remove existing functionality that is not related to auth scoping
return 200 for sessions owned by a different user
change the Abracapocus runtime, orchestrator, or backends

allowed: add Depends(get_current_user) to existing endpoint signatures
add user_id and companion_id fields to the session data model
forbidden: change existing endpoint URL paths or HTTP methods
remove existing session features (create, read, delete)
add new endpoints beyond what already exists
return 200 or 403 for sessions owned by a different user (use 404 to prevent enumeration)
